summary: First-person news feature on the Global Youth Summit for Climate Action held in Bern, Switzerland, on September 23, 2023, where young activists presented an ultimatum to political leaders. The author, a millennial, profiles attendees including activists, scientists, an agronomist, a diplomat and a developer, and describes workshops, a tech exhibition and networking. The central demand is integrating youth voices into policy-making, alongside environmental education and aggressive carbon emission cuts.
one_line: Report from the September 2023 Global Youth Summit for Climate Action in Bern, where young activists demanded a voice in climate policy.
key_facts: The Global Youth Summit for Climate Action took place on September 23, 2023, in Bern, Switzerland's capital.
Attendees included young people as young as 15, such as Maria Fernández from Colombia, who said "We are not just fighting for our future, we are fighting for our now."
Naveen Johar, a 21-year-old from India, articulated the summit's demands: comprehensive environmental education, aggressive carbon emission reductions, and transnational collaboration.
The summit's ultimatum is the integration of youth voices in policy-making, or face relentless global civil action.
Leila Karam, a Lebanese environmental scientist, moved from the laboratory to legislative halls, saying her work "could not stay confined to academic journals."
Themba Khumalo, a South African activist, described combating industrial pollution in Johannesburg's underprivileged communities.
Sofia Pereira, a young agronomist from Portugal, spoke at a sustainable agriculture workshop on carbon sequestering farming and crop diversification and on shaping careers around climate solutions.
Finn Nguyen, 24, led a breakout session on youth in climate diplomacy; he previously lobbied in youth networks for the Paris Agreement.
The 'Tech for Earth' exhibition showed prototypes of AI-driven recycling systems and mobile apps for carbon footprint tracking.
Jia Wong, a software developer from Singapore, created the app 'GreenStride', which combines data analytics with community-based conservation efforts.
The conference center was described as a modern architectural marvel built from a mosaic of renewable materials.
Evening activities included networking, impromptu climate marches and art installations, with links between remote villages in Kenya and classrooms in Oslo cited as examples of connectivity.
